rows.claim: nominal evaluation runs every user function once
rows.evidence: probe3.jl:21; every stage function and guard and handler once at Float64; the `ws_init` allocation runs twice, once in the nominal probes and again in the event probe
rows.note: probe3.jl C1: ws_init => 2, others 1; src/build.jl:1008 and 1266
rows.fix: Reword the cell to name the stage, guard and handler functions, or have `probe_events` reuse the workspaces `_nominal` allocated.

rows.evidence: src/model.jl:121; Model(deployment, T) calls activation(build, T), which derives and runs the activation step's user functions when the build holds none at T
rows.note: probe3.jl C2: activation(ProbeDual) runs y_state, y_direct, x_deriv, ws_init
rows.fix: Say that materialization runs no user code of its own and derives the activation at T (step 3) when the Build holds none.

rows.claim: the first three are the build and build(world) runs them
rows.evidence: src/build.jl:795; build runs the structure step and the nominal evaluation; the activation step runs in build only for scalars named in the `activations` keyword, else at first activation(build, T) request, e.g. in Model(deployment, T)
rows.fix: The first two are the build, and `build(world)` runs them. Activation at `T` follows on request, or at build for the scalars `activations` names.

rows.claim: the walk does the five steps in this order
rows.evidence: src/structure.jl:525; one pre-order pass does them per node: class read before the path is pushed, contracts at once, an assembly's faces and wires after its children; type clauses and the obligation check run after the walk
rows.fix: Reword to say the five are facts the one walk gathers, with faces and wires resolved per level after the children, and the type clauses and obligation check after the walk.

rows.claim: the did-you-mean list is the destination's input list
rows.evidence: probe4.jl:6; a destination typo's candidates are the resolved component's input and output faces together, not its input list alone
rows.fix: against the faces of the component the endpoint resolved to, inputs then outputs
